Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and agreed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Data residency: core customer data must remain within US regions for now.
- Encryption: must have in-transit and at-rest encryption. Customer prefers customer-managed keys (CMK) where feasible.
- Logging & monitoring: audit logs for inference requests, key usage, and admin actions; retention policy of 1 year minimum.

3) Schedule a security deep-dive with your security team to go through architecture and key management (Aditya) — propose 2/19 or a time that works for your team.
4) Confirm whether Dedicated or Private deployment is required for BYOK/HSM — customer to advise (Samantha/Andre).

Notes on our side: Redwood supports TLS 1.2+ for in-transit and AES-256 for at-rest as standard. We offer multiple deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) — CMK and HSM options vary by mode; details in the attached KMS doc.

Hi Samantha — quick technical answers ahead of the deep-dive. I'll walk through these on the call but wanted to give concrete answers you can share with your security team: 

1) Key custody / BYOK: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys where the CMK lives in the customer's cloud account (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). This gives you full administrative control and visibility. For Hosted (shared) deployment we provide a managed key option; we can discuss tradeoffs on multi-tenant.

2) HSM / EKM: We support HSM-backed keys via cloud KMS HSM tiers (e.g., AWS CloudHSM-backed KMS) and integrations with external key managers via KMIP in Private deployments. So you can bring keys backed by an HSM or use your existing EKM.

3) In-transit & at-rest: All traffic to Redwood endpoints is TLS 1.3 (fallback to TLS 1.2 as needed). Data at-rest is encrypted with AES-256. When using CMK, data encryption keys are wrapped by your CMK, so Redwood never has unwrapped key material.

4) Key rotation/backup: Rotation can be managed by your KMS policy. We do not hold unwrapped keys in persistent form. For rotation, Redwood verifies new keys are usable during rollout; there is no downtime for key rotations when configured correctly. We can provide a checklist for rotation steps per cloud provider.

5) Logging/audit: We emit key usage logs and request-level audit logs. In Dedicated/Private we can push logs to your logging endpoint (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Azure Monitor) or ship weekly exports. Retention is configurable; default example is 1 year, but we can extend for compliance requirements.

6) Dedicated vs Private: Compliance differences are primarily in network isolation and control plane separation. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and is better for air-gapped/on-prem setups. For most enterprise compliance, Dedicated (with CMK in your account) meets requirements, but we'll confirm based on your auditor's checklist.

I've attached a simple architecture diagram and the KMS options doc for reference: encryption-arch-diagram.png (see drive link) and redwood-kms-options.pdf. Suggest we schedule the security deep-dive on Thu 19 Feb at 10:00am PT — does that work for your team?
